license.name: MIT
license.publicationRule: Keep this attribution in the experiment package; do not publish the CF, snapshot, disposable infobases, or large raw logs.

businessTask.statement: An inventory write-off line must have a strictly positive quantity. A negative or zero quantity must not be postable because a write-off must never increase stock.
businessTask.currentBehavior: The document has no object-level quantity validation. Its manager aggregates the entered Quantity and writes it as an Expense movement. A negative expense increases the InventoryInWarehouses balance, and the existing negative-balance control does not reject that increase.
businessTask.expectedBehavior: Posting InventoryWriteOff is cancelled when any Inventory row has Quantity <= 0. Existing positive-quantity posting and insufficient-stock rejection remain unchanged.

sourceLocators.fact: Posting initializes document data, writes InventoryInWarehouses and InventoryCost movements, then calls negative-balance control; there is no BeforeWrite quantity validation.
The entered Inventory.Quantity is aggregated and emitted unchanged as an Expense movement for both inventory quantity and cost.
The register computes the current posting's net warehouse/product balance change and marks whether it changed.
The existing control cancels only when the resulting register balance is below zero; it does not reject a negative write-off quantity that increases the balance.
InventoryWriteOff is postable, records InventoryInWarehouses and InventoryCost, has a Warehouse, and has Inventory rows with Product and signed decimal Quantity.

dataCreationInsideEnterprise: Create three Products catalog items of ProductTypes.Inventory using that unit.
For each product, create and post an InventoryIncrease document for quantity 10 in the test warehouse.

Create a separate InventoryWriteOff document for each case, write it unposted, attempt posting, then query Document.InventoryWriteOff.Posted and AccumulationRegister.InventoryInWarehouses balance from the same disposable infobase.
scenario.oracle: A current-run receipt records created object identities, each document's stored Posted value, and queried register balance. Validation compares the complete receipt to the exact case expectations; successful process startup or file parsing alone is insufficient.
scenario.mutationCriterion: Removing the production patch must reproduce the target RED observation while both control cases still match their frozen expectations.

constraints: Source CF, snapshot, snapshot manifest, and live infobases are immutable; any actual write is a failed experiment even if bytes are restored.
All writes are confined to the declared new run roots under .local/ and to committed experiment documentation/tests.
RED and GREEN use the same scenario identity, data quantities, object types, oracle fields, and validator.
Production change is limited to the declared existing object module and is separate from test instrumentation.
No GUI, external integration, production data, secret, metadata-schema change, new framework, parser, runner, adapter, plugin, RAG, MCP, graph, or general write harness.
The experiment package may publish only minimal MIT-attributed diffs and sanitized bounded evidence, never the source CF, snapshot, infobases, private absolute paths, or large raw logs.
stopCriteria: The target RED observation cannot be reproduced on the exact immutable source.
The current issue #10 native runtime path cannot create the declared data or observe Posted and register balance without GUI.
Implementing the rule requires metadata-schema change, live data, secrets, production access, or writing an immutable input.
The production patch cannot remain inside the single allowed object module.
A legal/licensing decision beyond the recorded MIT attribution is required.
RED and GREEN cannot run the identical frozen scenario or current-run evidence cannot be distinguished from stale output.
